title: A module that is the directed union of flat modules over directed subrings is flat
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $(R_\lambda)_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ a family of subrings of $R$ indexed by a nonempty set $\Lambda$ with a partial order such that $R_\lambda\subseteq R_\mu$ for $\lambda\le\mu$, any two elements of $\Lambda$ have an upper bound, and $R= igcup_\lambda R_\lambda$. Let $M$ be an $R$-module (an $R_\lambda$-module by restriction of scalars for every $\lambda$). For every $\lambda$ let $M_\lambda$ be an $R_\lambda$-module and $\iota_\lambda:M_\lambda	o M$ an $R_\lambda$-linear map, and for $\lambda\le\mu$ let $t_{\lambda\mu}:M_\lambda	o M_\mu$ be an $R_\lambda$-linear map, such that $t_{\lambda\lambda}=\mathrm{id}$, $t_{\mu
u}\circ t_{\lambda\mu}=t_{\lambda
u}$ for $\lambda\le\mu\le
u$, and $\iota_\mu\circ t_{\lambda\mu}=\iota_\lambda$ for $\lambda\le\mu$. Assume (i) every element of $M$ is $\iota_\lambda(m)$ for some $\lambda$ and some $m\in M_\lambda$, and (ii) if $m\in M_\lambda$ and $\iota_\lambda(m)=0$, then $t_{\lambda\mu}(m)=0$ for some $\mu\ge\lambda$. If $M_\lambda$ is a flat $R_\lambda$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] for every $\lambda$, then $M$ is a flat $R$-module.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 05UU (lemma-colimit-rings-flat, algebra.tex line 8857), part (2), for the directed system of the subrings $R_\lambda$ with colimit $R$; conditions (i) and (ii) say that $(M,\iota_\lambda)$ is the colimit of the system $(M_\lambda,t_{\lambda\mu})$ (proof of 05UU uses Lemma Tag 00DB lemma-directed-colimit-exact). Tag verified in stacks-project/tags/tags (05UU,algebra-lemma-colimit-rings-flat). The existing node lem-weil-pbc-colimit-rings-flat states only part (1), with a single module flat over every $R_\lambda$

proof.text: *The ideal test and a common coefficient stage.* By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-fg-ideal-criterion], it is enough to prove that for each finitely generated ideal $\mathfrak a=(r_1,\ldots,r_n)\subseteq R$, multiplication $\mathfrak a\otimes_RM\to M$ is injective. Since $R=\bigcup_\lambda R_\lambda$, choose $\lambda_0$ containing all $r_i$ (use an upper bound repeatedly). For $\mu\ge\lambda_0$ put $\mathfrak a_\mu=(r_1,\ldots,r_n)R_\mu$. The upper set $J=\{\mu:\mu\ge\lambda_0\}$ is nonempty and directed, and cofinal in $\Lambda$: any $\lambda$ and $\lambda_0$ have a common upper bound. The ideals $\mathfrak a_\mu$ and modules $M_\mu$ restrict to directed systems on $J$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 05UU (lemma-colimit-rings-flat), proof: the finitely generated ideal descends to an index and the proof proceeds over indices above it; flatness test is Lemma Tag 00HD (lemma-flat)

proof.text:
*The colimits of the rings and ideals.* For $\mu\le
u$ in $J$, the maps $R_\mu\hookrightarrow R_
u$ and $\mathfrak a_\mu\hookrightarrow\mathfrak a_
u$ are inclusions. Their unions are respectively $R$ and $\mathfrak a$: every element of $R$ lies in some $R_\lambda$, hence in a common upper stage with $\lambda_0$; and an element $\sum_i s_ir_i$ of $\mathfrak a$ has finitely many coefficients $s_i$, all in one such stage. Consequently $R$ is the colimit of the $R_\mu$ as rings and as abelian groups, and $\mathfrak a$ is the colimit of the $\mathfrak a_\mu$ as abelian groups [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. The induced $R$-module structure on this ideal colimit agrees with multiplication in $R$, because each transition map is a ring inclusion.

proof.text:
*The tensor comparison.* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-tensor-varying-rings] to the systems $A_\mu=R_\mu$, $P_\mu=\mathfrak a_\mu$, $N_\mu=M_\mu$ on $J$. The transition maps on the ideals are semilinear by inclusion, and those on $M_\mu$ are semilinear by the hypothesis that $t_{\mu
u}$ is $R_\mu$-linear (the $R_\mu$-action on $M_
u$ is by restriction along $R_\mu\subseteq R_
u$). Steps 2 and 3 identify their colimits with $R$, $\mathfrak a$, and $M$ and identify the resulting module structures. Hence $\varinjlim_{\mu\in J}(\mathfrak a_\mu\otimes_{R_\mu}M_\mu)\cong\mathfrak a\otimes_RM$, taking the class of $y\otimes x$ at stage $\mu$ to $y\otimes\iota_\mu(x)$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 05UU (lemma-colimit-rings-flat), proof: the displayed multiplication map is the colimit of the maps $\mathfrak a'R_{i'}\otimes_{R_{i'}}M_{i'}\to M_{i'}$

proof.text: *Injectivity at each stage and passage to the limit.* For each $\mu\in J$, multiplication $h_\mu:\mathfrak a_\mu\otimes_{R_\mu}M_\mu\to M_\mu$ is injective: it is the inclusion $\mathfrak a_\mu\hookrightarrow R_\mu$ tensored with the flat $R_\mu$-module $M_\mu$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], followed by $R_\mu\otimes_{R_\mu}M_\mu\cong M_\mu$. These injections commute with transitions since $t_{\mu\nu}$ is semilinear. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-abelian-groups-exact], the induced map between their abelian-group colimits is injective. Under the identifications of steps 3 and 4 it is multiplication $\mathfrak a\otimes_RM\to M$, as both maps send the stage-$\mu$ class of $y\otimes x$ to $y\iota_\mu(x)$. Thus the ideal test of step 1 shows that $M$ is flat over $R$.
